title: Ontario Unveils 140-Point Scoring System for New Permanent Residence Pathways
excerpt: The province’s revamped immigration program will rank candidates across ten categories including work region, education, language proficiency, and compensation.
body:
• Ontario has published a 140-point scoring system that will rank candidates for provincial nomination under its new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream
  • Points are awarded across ten categories: work region, occupation skill level, compensation, occupational category, Ontario work experience, tax history, education, Canadian credentials, language proficiency, and temporary resident status
  • Jobs outside Toronto score the highest for work region, with Northern Ontario earning 15 points and Toronto earning zero
  • The Expression of Interest system remains closed but is expected to reopen later this summer

The Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program has revealed the scoring criteria it will use to rank candidates competing for provincial nominations for Canadian permanent residence, according to CIC News.

Published on July 20, 2026, the scoring system assigns up to 140 points across ten categories under Ontario’s new Ontario Workforce Priority Stream, which replaced all nine of the province’s previous immigration pathways in a sweeping overhaul that took effect June 26.

How the Scoring Works

The system heavily rewards candidates working outside the Greater Toronto Area. Northern Ontario positions earn the maximum 15 points for work region, while Eastern Ontario, Central Ontario outside the GTA, and Southwestern Ontario each earn 10 points. Jobs in the GTA but outside Toronto score 5 points. Toronto itself carries zero points — a clear signal that the province wants to distribute immigration benefits across its geography.

Compensation matters significantly. Workers earning $40 or more per hour receive the maximum 15 points, scaling down to zero for those earning less than $20 per hour. Occupation skill level adds up to 9 points for TEER 0 and TEER 1 roles, with TEER 4 and 5 positions receiving none.

Experience, Education, and Language

Ontario work experience in the position offered by the employer is worth up to 18 points for candidates with more than 24 months in the role. Other candidates with general Ontario work experience can earn up to 12 points. The system also rewards Canadian tax history, awarding 8 points to candidates with a highest annual income of $70,000 or above in the past five years.

Education is scored up to 10 points, with doctorates and medical degrees at the top. Canadian educational credentials receive a separate allocation of up to 10 points for those with two or more post-secondary Canadian credentials.

Language proficiency carries substantial weight. Candidates with a minimum Canadian Language Benchmark score of 9 or higher across all four abilities in English or French receive 15 points. Bilingual candidates who score at least CLB 6 in both official languages earn an additional 10 points.

Three Pathways Under One Stream

The scoring system applies across the three pathways within the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream:

The TEER 0–3 pathway targets workers in higher-skilled occupations requiring post-secondary education or training. The TEER 4–5 pathway opens a route for lower-skilled workers who meet specific employment requirements. The self-employed physicians pathway covers registered physicians eligible to bill through the Ontario Health Insurance Plan.

Self-employed physicians are scored using an alternate method for work experience and are not assessed on hourly wage.

What Candidates Need to Know

The province’s Expression of Interest system — where eligible candidates must register before being invited to apply — is currently closed. Ontario has said the new EOI system is “anticipated to open later in the summer,” though no specific date has been announced.

Foreign nationals who applied under the previous pathways will continue to have their applications assessed under the old rules. Those with existing EOIs in the pool will see them automatically withdrawn over the coming weeks as the platform is updated.

“The new regulations streamline pathways to permanent residence for individuals with arranged employment in Ontario.”

— Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program

What It Means for Indian Immigrants

Indian nationals consistently rank among the top applicants to Ontario’s provincial nominee program. The new scoring system’s emphasis on higher-skilled occupations, strong language proficiency, and Canadian education credentials could benefit the many Indian workers already established in Ontario’s technology, healthcare, and engineering sectors.

However, the zero-point allocation for Toronto — where a large share of the Indian diaspora is concentrated — may push candidates to consider employment opportunities in other parts of the province. Ontario’s three additional streams covering priority healthcare, entrepreneurs, and exceptional talent are expected in a second phase, for which no launch date has been announced.
